utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Theunens, although it may sound like a routine, it is not. But you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Kay, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we look at a document now, 65 ter 2618. And just to brief you on the subject that we're going to go through, we're going to look at various documents, pre-Operation Storm, relevant to the Knin garrison, as it was set up under Major Gojevic, all right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The first document is dated 1st of March, 1994, and we can see that it was a temporary assignment of Major Gojevic, as acting commander of the Knin garrison HQ. If we turn to page 2 of the English, we see that Major Gojevic was the commander of the Knin Home Guard Battalion.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And you remember that yesterday in our brief hour and a quarter, we looked at a document that referred to the Knin garrison being set up under the organisational order of work in the garrison, the particular districts that the garrison -- Knin garrison was going cover, and it referred to the Home Guard Battalion. You recollect that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And you see that Major Gojevic is the acting commander of Knin garrison.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That just sets the scene. Shall we go to the next document, which is 65 ter 4399. This is a document which actually has typing errors on the front page in the English. I'll warn the court. While it is coming up, may we admit the previous document into evidence, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that becomes Exhibit D994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D994 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Ah, we've got an improved translation from the original document that was in the 65 ter list, so no worries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is the 10th of November, 1994, some nine months before Operation Oluja. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, and I have also included this and the previous document in part 1 of the report, English page 99.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exactly. That's why I didn't ask whether you had seen them before. And this document, nine months before Oluja, assigns people to various positions, and we can see that on the page, that a number of appointments are made. So you would agree with me, if we turn to page 3 of the English that this is an attempt to start the establishment of the Knin garrison. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen any documents indicating that Major -- that General Gotovina or anybody else appointed another -- or a commander to the Knin garrison at an earlier moment. So based on the documents I reviewed, I agree with -- with your suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Because we know that the first appointment of the first document that we looked at arose as a result of the order dated the -- February 1993 to ensure continuity of work and command in the Split Military District, and these are the first appointments that are made. Agreed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And you'll notice there on the third page of the English we have Knin DB which refers to Knin Home Guard; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it, but DB should stand for, domobranska, and then battalion, so the Home Guard Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And we know that Major Gojevic was the Knin Home Guard commander.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, commander of the Knin Home Guard Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah. I don't know whether you can just deal with this general matter then. Nine months before Operation Storm, some personnel being assigned to this new position of the Knin garrison. Agreed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to these documents and as you have mentioned, the document appointing Gojevic refers to the February 1993 order, so that would suggest that he is the first acting garrison commander for the Knin garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In your report, you pointed out a number of functions that Major Gojevic undertook, and we will be looking at each and every document, and made various comments about the kind of tasks that Major Gojevic was undertaking.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And that can be found on English page 69 of part 1 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And we will going to those and having a look at them because those tasks that you were pointing out, weren't they actually tasks that Major Gojevic was doing as the Knin Home Guard commander but using his new title as the Knin garrison commander. The actual tasks themselves didn't fit with the duties and responsibilities of a garrison commander. We'll be looking at them in a moment, but I'm putting it to you in the round to see if that is something that you were aware of when writing your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can indeed conclude that the tasks I have derived from the documents I reviewed which can be found on English page 69, part 1 of the report, do not correspond with the tasks that are listed under paragraph 54 of D32. The main reason for that obviously is that the Knin garrison is not located in its establishment area, and therefore cannot carry out the duties one would expect it to implement because there is no garrison area at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us also look, and we will go it those documents in a moment, but what the position was with the other garrisons within the Split Military District, because you make a number of comparisons in your report, don't you, concerning what the Split garrison commander did and what his powers were?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have indeed included documents that provide information on the activities of the commander of the Split garrison; in particular, in the area of maintaining order and discipline, as it is foreseen in the doctrinal documents establishing the duties of garrison commanders in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And would it be right to say that you have included those documents of comparison with the Split garrison commander to draw a parallel as to what the Knin garrison commander should be doing?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly. The documents I mentioned in the previous reply can be found on English page 175, part 1 of the report, and I have used these documents to illustrate how a garrison commander, in that -- in this case, the Split garrison commander, carries out his duties in the area of maintaining order and discipline. I have not drawn a comparison or a parallel, as you call it, with what the acting commander of the Knin garrison was doing in that area. One of the reasons being that I didn't have specific documents on how the commander, or acting commander, of the Knin garrison was implementing his duties in the area of maintaining order and discipline prior to Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if there are no documents on that, that indicates he was doing nothing.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The fact that I don't have documents does not mean that nothing was done. I mean, the documents can exist but are not available to the OTP. Maybe there were no document, maybe the documents were destroyed, maybe he did nothing. So it is a possibility, but I don't think we can draw a simple conclusion as the one you are suggesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's see, shall we, and see who is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to the first document that I wish to produce. May the document we've just looked at be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D995, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D995 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we look at 2D07-0042.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 16th of February 1995 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, may I first seek some clarification on a previous ... The 10th of November documents which was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- on our screen a minute ago, you wanted to turn to page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In my version, I have got only two pages, I think, if I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- correct. So therefore I wonder if have I the wrong document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I remember I pointed out that I was using a document that had a typing error on it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say a previous version may be [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A previous version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour is quite right. It is now a two-page document correctly typed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 2D07-0042. First of all, Mr. Theunens, is this a document that you have seen before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, because otherwise I would have included it in my report, and I have no recollection that I included this document in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You certainly didn't. Shall we just start at the top of the left-hand corner, first of all. You notice the stamp and Republic of Croatia, Ministry of Defence, Croatian army Main Staff, garrison command, Split. Shall we deal with one matter in your report that you mentioned that indicated to you that General Cermak had some higher authority within the system, and that concerns the Knin garrison having above its title: Croatian army Main Staff. Do you recollect that part of your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is in the second part, English page 258. But I have not drawn the conclusion you are suggesting in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you read out what you say so that we are not ambiguous about it.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. So the title is: 4, Relations Between the Split Military District Command (Gotovina) and the Knin garrison Command (Cermak), 6th August to October 1995. Shall I also read out the introduction, or directly --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just read out what you wrote about the stamp.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. "(A), introduction, the functional relationship between Cermak and Gotovina while Cermak is the commander of the Knin garrison is not as clear-cut as what is set out in HV doctrine on the relations between garrison commanders and MD Commanders." And then I have a subtitle (B). So (A) is the introduction. (B) is the next title, that is Cermak's point of view. I have then a paragraph 1: "The written orders or other documents Cermak issues during his tenure of commander of the Knin garrison, discussed here above, do not make reference to the Split MD, but mention only the 'Croatian army Main Staff' as the superior command." Then there is a footnote. The next sentence: "On 8th of August a Split Military District unit stamp is issued to Cermak, following the order by Colonel -- General it should have been, Colonel General Ante Gotovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's just stop there. That's all we need now. But you will notice here that the Split garrison command is headed in the same way.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And every single garrison command is also headed in the same way, be they from Imotski [phoen], Benkovac, Zadar, Sinj, is headed the same way?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure for all the other garrisons. We would have to look at documents. But I agree with you that, for example, 65 ter 5781 and 5782 which are documents issued by the commander of the Split garrison do not mention the Split Military District in their heading, and -- yeah, indeed, that's -- corresponds with what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We should be picking up a few more examples on our way. But it's -- it's right, then, that the point you were making in your report is wrong.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not entirely agree, because I find it interesting in the context of -- of discussing the relations between Generals Cermak and Gotovina, to see that based on the documents I reviewed, General Gotovina orders to issue a Split Military District stamp to General Cermak. I have not drawn any particular conclusion on the fact that the heading in the left top or the letterhead of the orders and reports issued by General Cermak do not mention the Split Military District, but I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I just stop you there.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention in your report that the Split garrison also had the same heading, that the Zadar garrison has the same heading, so that it wasn't giving an impression that the Knin garrison was somehow different? Why didn't you point that out to these Judges?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I hadn't seen any documents indicating that General Gotovina ordered to hand over or to hand out a stamp with mentioning of Split Military District to these other garrisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's nothing to do with the stamp. It's to do with the heading: Main Staff. Please don't try and divert the attention, Mr. Theunens. It is to do with that sentence about the Main Staff. Not the stamp. The stamp is entirely different. The stamp is the number, 3231. It's about the heading: Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I see your point, and if the wording as it is in the report now is misleading, then I'm willing to amend it in order to avoid any misunderstandings on that aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think you have corrected it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not entirely clear to me now, Mr. Theunens. I do understand that orders from other garrisons, not Knin garrison, have the same letterhead. You were asked why you did not point at this. It's not clear to me whether you would draw similar conclusions as you did, right or wrong, in relation to the Knin garrison, because, if so, there would be no reason to refer to the others being exactly the same and justifying the same conclusions. If, however, that would mean something different for you, especially in relation to the Knin garrison, then I understand the question why you did not clarify that. So it's not entirely clear to me at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will try to clarify it. I was under the understanding when I saw the order by General Gotovina for the stamp that this was a stamp that could be used for the letterhead in the reports and orders, the letterhead used by the Knin garrison. Following Mr. Kay's clarification, I realize that was probably a wrong conclusion from my side, i.e., that the stamp, Split Military District, or the unit stamp Split Military District, was not intended for the letterhead used by the Knin garrison in its written communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I have to relate your observations primarily to the heading in the report which says: Cermak's point of view; that the fact that Mr. Cermak was not using the stamp issued to him has no significance, although you suggested that it had some significance. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. Because I was under the erroneous understanding that the stamp had relevance for the letterhead, but after clarification the stamp was not to be used in the letterhead but for other purposes now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The say the clarification is what one would find in the letterhead of other garrisons. Have you verified that, or have you just accepted that from Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I checked on a -- actually on one document -- no, at least two documents from the Split garrison, and there indeed there is it no reference made to the Split Military District. I'm willing of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you. I'm just trying to verify for myself exactly on what basis you made this distinction and what it actually means here. I now do understand. Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's look at the letter that is written, because I have asked you certain questions about the functioning capacity that would have been possible from the Knin garrison, and we see on the 16th of February, 1995 this letter, which is from the Split garrison commander, Mr. Zoricic. If we go to page 3, we can see that, and then can we go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: With Your Honours' leave I'm trying to enable as much information to come before the court in that way. Can we go back to beginning now as we see that this is from the garrison commander, Colonel Zoricic, whom you had referred to in cross-examination by Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He has written to the chief of the Main Staff, General Bobetko at that time, and the subject is on the functioning of the Split garrison. And it says: "In practice, the Split garrison has still not been completely put into operation, especially in establishing command, cooperation, coordination, and security of complete work, order, and discipline in the garrison." If we just stop there for a moment. You agree that the Split garrison, of course, was an established entity at a garrison that was in existence within the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's not the Knin situation. We can see that he refers to the order with which it was established, that the work of the garrison shall be based on the rules of service, and he refers to certain problems in practical work and that commanders are obliged to define concrete tasks. He says: "It has not been done so far." And that's relevant to those questions I've asked you about Major Gojevic's preparations in advance. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this document addresses the functioning of the Split garrison. It does not address the functioning of the Knin garrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand Mr. Kay uses it is as a comparison to the stage of development of the operations of a garrison. Was that clear to you? I'm just checking whether you understood the question as I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You remember yesterday I showed you a document dated the 20th June 1995, 28th of June, 1995, where we saw current manpower for Knin garrison was three. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember. But I'm just -- I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're going through every paragraph in this letter, by the way, so you can see what the Split garrison was facing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I had some concern whether Mr. Theunens exactly understood what you were aiming and give him an opportunity to tell us what he apparently has on his lips at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do understand also from other documents; for example 65 ter 5781 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall we pull that up, then? Because I want to see what you're referring to. Is it necessary for us to pull that up and look at to see the point?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I can just say what I want to say and then you decide whether you want to see the document or not. Because I can do it in two lines. 65 ter 5781 and 5782 are actually the cover page and a report called, Records Of The Work And Disciplinary Analysis Meeting of the Split garrison, dated May 1995, where --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We'll be looking at all these. Don't worry.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just follow me, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, it's -- that's good guidance for the witness. At the same time, Mr. Theunens, if there's anything in the course of what Mr. Kay puts to you, if there's anything missing, if you just make a small note that you want to draw attention to a certain matter, and then after we have finished a chapter of the cross-examination, you will be given, by Mr. Kay -- I take it, you will take the initiative, Mr. Kay, to give you an opportunity to add anything that has not been dealt with and you consider to be important. Because if we continue to say that you want to say something, and Mr. Kay says don't be afraid, it will be there, then that might create some unrest which better be avoided. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We'll go -- if you follow my route, Mr. Theunens, it's not a document you've seen before, and I suggest you read it and you think about it. So let's go through what he says in February 1995, six months before Operation Storm. Next paragraph: "Commands are obliged to provide garrison commands with all necessary material and means in order to enable efficient work in the garrison. It has not been done either." Next paragraph : "Commanders are obliged to control work, order, discipline in the garrison ..." refers to a quarterly analysis. "Something similar has never been done in Split garrison, established 1993." Let's go to page 2. He says, in his view, the Split garrison was not established on the basis of the organisational order. It's a question I have put to you about Knin. "Another practical problem is the authority of the garrison commander, garrison control officer, and garrison duty officer. I have no authority over military police, and I do not even cooperate with them, since the garrison institution has been ignored by the 72nd Military Police Battalion commander. Without the assistance and possibility of using military police, it is impossible to reach the required level of order and discipline." Let's just stop there. That's a very important matter, don't you think, in relation to the evidence that you have been submitting to the Court concerning the institution of the garrison. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is important, but I do consider that this information should change any of the conclusions I draw in relation to relations between garrison commanders and military police because the conclusions I draw applied to different situations. And if you want, can I draw your attention to -- I mean for the situation prior to Storm, to 65 ter 5626, whereby Generals or Colonel Zoricic asks the 72nd Military Police Battalion, if I'm not wrong, in March 1995 to provide manpower for the monitoring as well as the maintaining of law and order during a football game between Hajduk Split and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's the next document we are going to look at. I'm putting all the documents in, Mr. Theunens. There is no concealment. Your footnotes have been studied. They have been then be analysed and further materials, mainly from the Prosecution, assembled, all right? But surely would you agree this paragraph and this letter would have had to have featured as an important explanation by you to the Judges in this Court, in relation to the subject matter of your expertise. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told you earlier, if I had had a document I would have included it, and [indiscernible] 65 ter 5781 and 5782, but they basically say the same about relations between the Split garrison commander and the 72nd Military Police Battalion, and these two 65 ters numbers refer to a document of May 1995 and are included in the addendum of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When he says he has no authority over the military police, that is because those laws that we looked at yesterday do not, in fact, give him power to order the military police. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would disagree with that interpretation because if indeed the garrison commander had no powers over the military police, he would not address the chief of the Main Staff to discuss that problem because it is a non-existing problem. It is only because he -- he sees that the laws and regulations are not being implemented, that as one would do in the military, he -- the garrison commander, consults in this case, the most senior officer, i.e., the chief of the Main Staff, to inform him of the problems he is facing in -- with the aim of having these problems solved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let me try to understand your testimony in relation to this question. Mr. Kay asks you whether you would agree with him that the garrison commander says that he has no authority over the military police, and Mr. Kay suggests to you that -- that that is because the legislation in force doesn't give him such powers. Your answer is about another matter. Your answer is about someone who complains that he sees all kind of problems which he can't solve because he has no authority over the military police. Isn't it, that is your answer. Now that can mean two things. First it is wrong that I have no authority over the police; or I have no authority over the police, could someone do something in order to resolve these problems because I can't, isn't it? Now everything whether right or wrong comes down to whether he has these powers under the existing legislation, and that appears to be a question which you have not answered. So let's first look at the formal legislative framework and see whether that any power is granted to a garrison commander, any exercise of authority over the military police. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Article 9 of P880 does not mention the garrison commander. So that is correct. However, it states that in addition to the military district commander, commander of the navy or commander of the air force, the military police is for the implementation of the regular military police tasks subordinated to the highest -- excuse me, to the highest HV officer in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By function. The translations were amended, Mr. Theunens. It's by function. There was an old translation before the Court, and it was amended during the testimony of the witness -- after the witness Dzolic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm willing to accept that. I was surprised that I am only informed of that now. But, anyway. Now from other documents I have seen, for example, the document about the football game, I agree it is only one document, but it suggests that a garrison commander, i.e., the Split garrison commander in March 1995 can request the military police to provide him with assistance in order to maintain order and discipline in the city during a football game.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that Mr. Kay will take to you that document and request order, authority, might be an issue to be discussed there, but I -- But therefore you say, on the basis of Article 9 of which apparently the translation you worked with is not a correct one and that seems to be agreed upon by the parties, Mr. Waespi, from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I will check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You will check that. Yes, from the reference to the highest -- let me just ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Article 9 is in the rules concerning the military police, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The highest HV officer, that's for you, and you're now informed about the translation not being fully correct, that's for you the basis to say that there is some basis in the law for the exercise of authority. That's an answer to Mr. Kay's question. Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, that is totally wrong, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... just wanted to establish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least it answers your question and that was my first question. The answer would be about what you asked the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Article 9 doesn't make the garrison commander more senior by function to other commanders of brigades, battalions, Military Districts, whatever, does it? The garrison commander is way down in the scale. You're bluffing, Mr. Theunens, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, I think that you should review my answer because I have never made any suggestions about the level of the garrison commander anywhere in the scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was implicit in your answer to His Honour Judge Orie that, under Article 9, the commander of the military police would report to the garrison commander and that that would mean that what Mr. Zoricic, Colonel Zoricic, was saying was wrong in law.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation of this paragraph here on the relations Colonel Zoricic has with the military police, to me, shows that the lack of authority he has over the military police is not as a result of a total absence in the law of -- sorry of a total absence of a basis for such authority in the regulations but is due do his -- due to the situation is he facing, in particular, his relationship with the commander of the 72nd Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We've got many more documents to come, so I'm not going to stay further on this, because the reporting line will be a matter we'll be looking at, at one of the occasions over the next few days. Let's just have a look at further matters here. Under proposal of the solution, so what you said about him taking up the matters of authority is being followed by him to a very high level, wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I agree because I would expect Colonel Zoricic to first address the matter with the commander of the Split Military District, as the latter is according to the doctrine responsible for the order and discipline in the garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Of course you don't know whether he has or hasn't.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the basis of that document or this document, I mean what I have seen from the document, we cannot draw that conclusion. There doesn't seem to be a reference to an earlier discussion by Colonel Zoricic and General Gotovina of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You can't -- draw any conclusions about it from this document, and if we look at it in number three of his proposals he says -- and I want you to look at this very carefully as it is directly relevant to those matters you were talking about before you'd studied this document. "The garrison commander shall be given authority and one military police company in the city of Split area shall be subordinated to him." He is asking for powers over the military police. He is saying, That is a solution to the problem. Wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And it is important to note that he suggest to have a military police company subordinated to him on a permanent basis, which goes even further than being in a position to exercise authority over the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He asks for authority and to have a company subordinated to him. Let's move then --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document become an exhibit, Your Honour, unless the Court is wanting to look at that time further.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D996 is admitted into evidence. And, Mr. Theunens, you specifically pointed at the fact that a military police company subordinated to him in a -- on a permanent basis, which suggests that, although on a not permanent basis, he exercised already authority over the military police. Where do we read that, or what makes you conclude that what he asks for is not being granted authority at all, but authority -- but then on a different basis. Where I do find this in the wording of this letter? Because I read under 3: "The garrison commander shall be given authority, and one military police company in the city ... shall be subordinated to him," which suggests that he has no authority and that he has no unit subordinated to him. Nevertheless, you give it a different explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say, Your Honours, is that in his proposal, Colonel Zoricic says that he should be given authority, i.e., should be allowed to issue orders or make requests to the military police. When I say "make requests," it is, for example, to ask for manpower for specific task related to the maintaining of order and discipline. So that, for example, Colonel Zoricic can ask well, Can I have a section of military policemen for a week or for a few days for this specific activity I foresee, which is aimed at maintaining order and discipline within the district, or within the garrison, I apologise, whereby he requests the manpower from the command of the military police battalion, but it doesn't mean that he needs to have an entire company subordinated to him on a permanent basis. Why? Because if he would have a company subordinated to him -- and I add the word permanent because his request does not include the mentioning of temporarily or for a specific time-period. He just says subordinated to the garrison command, well, if he has his own military police company, he doesn't have to send such a request for manpower to the battalion commander, i.e., the commander of the military police battalion. That's why I made the distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But my question was, where in this document or where in any related document we find support for this analysis of -- because what you say is to be given authority means to be given authority to make requests. Now, the difference -- but that is -- I'm not a native-speaking person, but authority and requesting, usually people are -- do not need much authority to make a request. I can make requests to anyone as long as it's not -- so therefore you give a very specific meaning to these words where I'm asking you on what basis exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, when we go to the top of the page ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second paragraph : "Another practical problem is the authority of the garrison commander. I have no authority over military police." And then Zoricic says a bit further, "since the garrison institution has been ignored by the 72nd Military Police Battalion command. Of course everybody can make a request, but in the military when you make a request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then first analyse that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it reads as follows: "I have no authority over military police, and I do not even cooperate with them, since the garrison institution has been ignored by the 72nd Military Police Battalion commander." Which at least raises the following issue: Whether the -- the fact that the garrison institution was ignored had an effect on cooperation, cooperation alone, or also on authority. If someone ignores that I exist, he might not be inclined to cooperate with me because he just ignores my existence. With authority it might be different that if I ignore the institution of the garrison, if the garrison would have authority over me, that it's just a matter of enforcing that authority. So that sentence is -- leaves open quite a few questions. For example, what makes you conclude that it's rather about the authority than about the cooperation that the ignoring of the institution of the garrison is relevant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not -- or I don't think I drew that conclusion. What I'm trying to explain is the word "authority" in this context means that when the district commander -- excuse me, the garrison commander sends a request to the commander of the 72nd Military Police Battalion for assistance, for example, manpower for a particular activity, authority means that actually the request will be granted except if there are really good reasons for the 72nd Military Police Battalion not to grant the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it is not formal authority but authority informally that to take serious what someone says who is in a certain position. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. Maybe it has to do with the difference between military language and civilian language, but in the military language if you make a request, in this context, i.e., from the garrison commander to the military police, the garrison commander expects the military police to fulfil that request. Now, we see a reference to that garrison commander considers that he is being ignored by the 72nd Military Police Battalion. In this particular context of the request, I conclude that actually the 72nd Military Police Battalion commander is not even answering to the request, doesn't even send a reply, doesn't say, well, impossible, or possible, or, well, you have no doctrinal basis or legal basis for making this request. Based on this paragraph here, it seems that the commander of the 72nd Military Police Battalion simply doesn't answer. Now, authority can also mean that, again -- and that will be based on a request, the military police battalion can assist the garrison commander in other areas. Not specifically with the provision of manpower, but, for example, if the commander of the garrison -- and that is actually what is explained in 5782. He invites representatives of the units in the Split garrison to attend the regular meeting or analysis. It's a monthly meeting. The monthly meeting on the analysis of the disciplinary situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we're moving away a bit from my question at this moment. I leave it to Mr. Kay to continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We looked yesterday at D34, which set out the fact, and that's the 27th of August 1993 organisational order regarding work, order and discipline at garrison HQs, Exhibit D34, paragraph 2: "The garrison headquarters do not have an operational function and the right to issue orders to Croatian army units, except precisely prescribed authorities regarding work, order, and discipline at the garrison headquarters outside of barracks," et cetera. And that is quite clear as to the authority or power of the garrison commander, in relation to the issuing of orders, that they have to be precisely prescribed authorities, and as I questioned you yesterday, those are the regulations, the laws of the garrison concerning order, discipline, do not cross the bridge at more than 30 kilometres an hour, other life of the garrison rules that are required of the garrison commander. Isn't that right, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But one of the -- I mean, the basic principle if you impose rules, that is, that you are also in a position to verify whether they are abided by. And the military police is one of the tools you can use as a garrison commander to verify as to whether your orders which apply to the disciplinary situation outside of the barracks are abided by, yes or no. And that requires that you have what is here described as authority over the military police. For example, that you request the military police to post a few men at your bridge to verify the speed at a specific date for a specific time-period which is something else than having a military police company subordinated to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You can request that, but the military police commander may accept it or reject it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But as I explained earlier, in the situation as it is prescribed by the rules, the commander of the military police - in this case a battalion - will have to explain why he rejects or why he cannot fulfil the request. That exactly explains also why Colonel Zoricic is addressing the chief of the Main Staff with the particular problems he is facing with the command of the 72nd Military Police Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn to page 7 of Exhibit D34 and look at paragraph 17, it was one I didn't produce before the Court yesterday in the interests of time, but maybe this will be the moment to -- to look at it, because it says -- there we are. Under regulating order, discipline, and supervision of conduct of military personnel, how the garrison commander shall lay down those instructions and what they cover: Working hours; time of exchange of internal service organs; conduct of military personnel in public places; type of supervision of conduct at the ZM through patrols, et cetera; restricted locations; use of public transport, et cetera. Exactly the type of issues that I was putting to you yesterday afternoon about regulating behaviour to ensure good order of the armed services within the garrison area. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And I would just like to draw the Trial Chamber's attention to the fact that for the fourth bullet, type of supervision of the conduct of people in the garrison area, mention is made of military police patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. No mention of orders but just how the instructions are to be laid down. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But as I explained in -- in the military -- an order or an instruction without mechanisms to verify its implementation will not be very effective. I mean, if you're talking about your bridge and speed limits, if you don't check whether that order is implemented and if you don't -- cannot convince those using the bridge that indeed there with can be speed checks and that indeed there will be measures taken against those who violate the 30-kilometre speed limit, I think we can be pretty sure that there will be many violations of the 30-kilometre speed limit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems to keep you apart. And that is -- the first one is the authority to lay down instructions and the authority to supervise the enforcement of such instructions, which you put on the same level and you, Mr. Kay, you do not say that much at this moment but at least that is not included as Mr. Theunens suggests.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also noticed that that's specific, and that is what Mr. Theunens draws your attention to, that the military police patrols as subject of a regulation on the type of supervision is mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean -- the points seem to be clear to me in this respect at this moment on this subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's just look at this, Mr. Theunens, as you told us were an experienced military officer. What we're looking at here are peacetime matters when the garrison and the military structure is in circumstances of being non-operational. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with that because we have, of course, the appointment of General Cermak to the position of the commander of the Knin garrison, and then I think it's at the end of -- I mean, the formal end of Operation Storm, even though there are still skirmishes with isolated enemy resistance pockets, as well as operations along the border of Bih, that an order given by General Cervenko to the military district commanders to establish the territorial organisation, i.e., to have garrison commanders appointed and the structures established in what is described as the newly liberated areas, and I remember the appointment of -- I believe it is captain or Major Ashley Minak to the position of --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We'll be looking at that. Do you think you are being unduly legalistic and relying on analysis and leaving common sense about how the military functions in giving this Court your opinions about those matters?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honours, I have tried to adopt the opposite approach, when drafting my report and also providing answers during my testimony. It is correct that I took the regulations as a starting point, but then the documents that describe the situation as it was during Storm are actually, in my view, more important as a basis to draw conclusions upon than purely the regulations. Looking at the regulations without looking at their implementation may be useful for what you call a legalistic discussion but is not a purpose of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you discussed this with more experienced military officers than yourself or garrison commanders or people with experience of these situations, as to what should be expected of a garrison in these circumstances. Have you discussed it --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please explain what you mean by "these circumstances."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you -- have you discussed whether in a conflict circumstances where a garrison is not set up, where the rules of the garrison are shaped for peacetime rather than the circumstances we have in Knin in August, September, October, and November 1995? Have you taken advice? Yes or no? It's simple.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but you're making a number of suggestions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Kay puts a question whether you have taken advice. Whatever his suggestions are in his question talking about legalistic or being lawyers, the Chamber, of course, is not unaware of what he suggests, but he doesn't seek confirmation of the suggestions. He seeks an answer and whether you did seek advice, yes or no. And how to deal the suggestions I think, just as Mr. Kay said several times to you, wait, just trust me, that I had not overlook anything, same is you don't have to be afraid that the Chamber will overlook suggestions which were not directly put to you for confirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the compilation of my report, I have not taken specific advice or sought specific advice as to the functioning of garrisons in peacetime or wartime. I do wish to mention that I attended a conference in Oslo in September which is, of course, after the filing of the report where there were members also of the British military, military prosecutors, and other people who deal with legal issues in the armed forces and where we had discussions -- I mean, informal discussions about the difficulties military commanders face when they have to maintain law and order -- I mean, military discipline, sorry, maintain military discipline among their forces during different types of conflicts because I think it is also important to make a distinction between the different types of conflicts we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The question is about the garrisons. There are many big issues you discuss elsewhere, Mr. Theunens, please confront the issues because it is the garrison that I'm concerned with. That's what's on trial here. You have you taken advice about whether the rules concerning garrisons apply more to a peacetime situation, a regular set of circumstances, rather than the situation we have here.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not taken, as I mentioned specific advice as to the functioning of garrisons. I wish to add that the documents -- I mean, the Croatian doctrinal documents I reviewed do not indicate that there is a difference, as suggested by Mr. Kay, in the functioning or role or other procedures that apply to garrisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us turn to 65 ter 5626, which is the document you wanted to -- to look at dated 27th of February, 1995, and arises 11 days after the letter to the Chief of Staff by Colonel Zoricic. And there we see the stamp again at the top left-hand corner about the Main Staff. The 27th of February. This is a subject: Order, to the 72nd Military Police Battalion, to the commander: "In order to control the conduct of military personnel in public places and to improve discipline, the Split garrison commander shall personally exercise control during the day during the football match with the assistance of the military police and supervisory officer." Note the heading order, but note what comes next: "You are requested to provide two military policemen to assist the Split garrison commander, Colonel Zoricic, and the supervisory officer on the 1st of March." We can see the terms there. The next page which we have no need to look at is signed Split garrison commander, Colonel Zoricic. First of all, do you know if Colonel Budimir, the commander of the 72nd Military Police Battalion, did provide the officers to Colonel Zoricic. Do you know?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I have not seen any documents indicating whether this order was abided by or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Secondly, do you agree that, in fact, if the Split garrison commander was to make any order, if he was to make any order, right or wrong, instead of issuing it against the commander of the 72nd, he should have issued it against the commander of the 1st Company of the Split Military Police. That would be the appropriate method, don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends of the relation that exists between the Split garrison command and the 1st Company of the Split Military Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you can't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the -- the manner how the question is asked now, no, I can't. I can only assume that Colonel Zoricic, as a senior officer, knew why he addressed the order to the commander of the 72nd Military Police Battalion and not as you suggest to the commander of the 1st company of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having looked at the previous document, dated the 16th of February, and then this document, dated the 27th of February, are you aware whether Colonel Zoricic was, in fact, trying to push an argument with the commander of the 72nd, Colonel Budimir?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I do not think that this document allows to -- to draw such conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us look at the terms of the document. It's headed order. You yourself have said several times to Mr. Misetic, one document doesn't make to establish that something is right, that if you take one document, that it proves necessarily the case. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. It depends of the nature of the document and the contents, and if the contents is -- is appears to be incoherent with what is established in the other documents discussing the same issue or related issues, then there should be a good reason or one would have to investigate why one particular document appears to indicate or suggest a totally different situation from what has been established in other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is no other document like this that you have seen. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean like --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. Just yes or no, otherwise we're going to be here following Christmas, I can promise you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, that is however -- if you say a "document like this," could be anything, could be about documents -- about football matches, could be documents signed by Mr. A or Mr. B, could be documents in which an order is presented as a request. Could be anything. So, therefore, the witness may inquire with you what you meant by "like this."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think the witness understands, Your Honour, the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently, if from his answers it becomes clear that he does understand, then, of course, we'll ask ourselves what the reason is that he further inquires into the matter. Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If the question is whether I have seen other orders by Colonel Zoricic to the 72nd Military Police Battalion, then, indeed, the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see any documents in which a garrison commander orders request bits for assistance of military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To assist them in this task.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have, Your Honours, and these are, for example, documents that or orders or requests issued by General Cermak when he is the commander of the Knin garrison between the 5th of August, 1995, and approximately November 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at this document, it's, in fact, not a proper order, is it, because he says, You are requested.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, the use of the term "requested" is a reflection of what has been discussed first in relation to Article 9 of the MP rules and then, more specifically, what was addressed by Colonel Zoricic under the -- in the paragraph on his authority over the military police. And he could have said, You are ordered. He says, You are requested, but above it, it says order, and in the subject it also says order. So for a military person this should be clear, whether he requests or whether he orders, the result Zoricic wants to achieve is the same. He wants the military police to provide him manpower to assist with the task described in the document, and he further more, the use of the term military policemen shall report to the supervisory officer at the garrison command at 1700 hours is another indication that he expects the military police to do something he has requested/ordered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There it is. Let move now, having admitted it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this go into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D997, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D997 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think it's the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's at least a quarter to 4.00. We will have a break, and we will resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the next document we can look at is P1120, which is the sort of document you wanted to look at, dated the 27th of February, 1995. And it's a subject: Annual analysis of the state of order, work, discipline and unusual incidents. We can see on the first page that it's to be conducted for the Split Military District in reviewing 1994 in the barracks in Sibenik. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, or at least with similar documents talking about the same analysis which is to be held.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I said you'd have an opportunity to look at these documents. And it is setting up what will take place in the meeting, who's to be there, and due to shortage of time, if we can just go to page 6 in the English. I don't think it bears any further examination other than the fact it is just a meeting arranged by which the Split Military District reviews the subject matter for the year. Obviously very important, but the point of me bringing it to your attention, because it's linked with other questions I have asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to the page before the programme there. On mine it's page 6. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just there, you'll notice the participants. You'll notice left-hand corner, Zborno Mjestos, the garrisons who are listed to attend. No ZM Knin. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Indicating that Knin garrison out of the loop in relation to this conference. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there's also follow-up document in relation to this conference, just to check whether they are included there. Because sometimes, even though it shouldn't be, but sometimes addressees are missed, but, yeah, I have no reason not to believe what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You hadn't noticed this, then, I take it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no specific recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document become an exhibit. Your Honour, I have many documents to go through, and I'm using my judgement on what I need to go into for the purposes of my cross-examination. The Court can look at the full content, and I'm trying to give a general description on the way if that meets with the Court's approval.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we get lost, we will let you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful. And may that be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, sorry, too much talking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think if we check P1121.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're going to that now. Exhibit P1121, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And P1121, which is a report to the commander personally about that conference that we have looked at, and an unsatisfactory level of order and discipline was established primarily concerning, we can see there, what is listed. Page 2 -- ah, leave this page here because it gives the flavour of the document about the experiences, lessons, and views to be obtained. If we now go to the last page where I answer your question. Knin ZM not included within the people circulated with this information. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. And the Benkovac garrison is not included either, as is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Don't worry --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As is Dubrovnik, Imotski, Vrgorac garrison, they're not included.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We don't need to go further into it.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can look at the next document, 65 ter 3438.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 22nd of March, 1995. And you see it's from military post Knin 3231. And we've no need to go to the end yet, but it's from Major Gojevic, and it's to the Split Military District Command and it's his report on jobs and duties in the period between November 1994, March 1995, and it's a document with which you're familiar; is it not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I have included that report --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, this concerns steps taken by him. And if we turn to page 2, we can see the kinds of jobs. And turning to page 3. And it's something that I raised with you earlier in cross-examination, about, in fact, how these reports actually indicate more what he is doing as the commander of the Knin Home Guard, rather than the garrison commander of Knin, which you agreed with. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I would also like to draw your attention to paragraph 6 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's why I have put it there, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it is obvious that -- I mean, the tasks you first showed, listed under paragraph 4, appear to be more in relation to his duties as commander of the Knin Home Guard Battalion, which from the military point of view is logical because there is no functioning Knin garrison command at that stage as Knin is still under Serb control. However, as we can see in paragraph 6, for example, Major Gojevic is attending a training course, training course related to activities of garrison headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: One matter I'm interested in, in relation to your report when you identify the tasks that acting commander of the Knin garrison, Major Gojevic is doing, you refer to collecting intelligence, you refer to the duties he is doing as commander of the Knin Home Guard, as to why you didn't make it clear in your report that those were not tasks and duties of a garrison commander but consistent with his position as the commander of the Knin Home Guard, why you didn't make that distinction but chose to point out features as to what he was doing pre-Oluja.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not include any specific conclusion on the aspects you indicate because I considered it logical that the acting commander of the Knin garrison could not implement the tasks determined in the regulations on the garrisons commanders at a stage when the Knin garrison was actually not existing, i.e., there was a formal structure, but it was located somewhere else. And as you can see from paragraph 54, the duties are -- the duties of a garrison commander are mainly territorial, i.e., maintain order and discipline outside the barracks, well, Gojevic could not implement these duties as long as the Knin garrison had not been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The purpose of question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, it would assist me if you put to the witness why he described a certain matter and not pay attention to another relevant element in your view. It would assist me to know exactly on what page to find that so that we can --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's page 69, on part 1 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was just putting it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And basically this is under the heading "Relationship Between Garrison Commanders and Military District Commanders," where I have an introduction referring to D33, and then I explain, okay, we see that garrison commanders are required to keep the Military District Commanders to whom they are required to keep the military district commanders to whom they are subordinated informed of their activities, and I list the reports Major Gojevic sends to General Gotovina prior to Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, it interests me why you referred to gathering information, intelligence, participation in operations, and you didn't make clear that that was not part of the garrison command's duties?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have answered that question. In my view, as long -- based on the tasks of a garrison commander as established in doctrine on the one hand, on the other hand, at that moment in time, the Knin garrison is not operating as a -- as a regular garrison, because Knin is under the control of the Serbs. The logical --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The point is whether you agree that this is potentially misleading, in relation to garrison commanders, because the heading concerns the relationship between garrison commanders, Military District Commanders, and then these features of an operational nature are put in your report. And anyone reading this may be led to believe that that is part of their tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honours, because I have explained these tasks at an earlier stage in my report, referring to the doctrinal regulations. I have also explained at an earlier stage in my report that the Knin garrison is not operating as a regular garrison, i.e., it is still located in Gospic, pending its move. Same applies to the Benkovac garrison. So I don't think that this is misleading. And, now, if anyone is mislead, it was certainly not my intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document after this is made an exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D998, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D998 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 3rd of April, 1995. It is from Colonel Zoricic again, and it's a call to a meeting and a requirement or call to a meeting. "All independent unit commanders are called to attend a regular monthly meeting at which ... orderliness, operations, and discipline shall be analysed." Is this a document you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I have seen this specific document, but the 5718 and 5782 deal with a similar issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Again, this is a meeting organised by the garrison commander on the subject that it speaks to. As part of the work of that garrison commander, he was able to undertake in Split at that time. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it's not question just a question of being able to undertake. This falls among his duties as established in the 1993 regulations. And I would also like to mention that this was the copy that was sent to the 72nd Military Police Battalion, as we can see from the stamp on the right top corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Why I put the question this way is that all these documents that you produce on this matter in your report are all pre-Operation Oluja. Did you appreciate that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the report -- the report is established in two parts. The documents on the way how the garrison commands are operating and how garrison commanders are implementing these -- their tasks prior to Operation Oluja are all included in part 1 of the report. I have not come across, for example, a document by Colonel Zoricic on a similar meeting during or after Operation Oluja. If I had come across such documents, I would have included them, probably in the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why I put the question that way is because of those questions I asked you about earlier today concerning the different situation, after Operation Oluja, to the situation that existed pre-Operation Oluja, and the examples in your report of the running of a garrison in a particular way, all your footnotes giving these types of documents are all pre-Oluja, no documents of this nature post-Operation Storm. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we turn to page 2 of this document, we will see, again, the Knin ZM and other garrisons not included within the list of units to attend.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I think that is logical because we're talking here about an invitation or an order for an invitation by the commander of the Split garrison, and as garrisons are -- can be defined as territorial commands, there is no reason for the commander of the Split garrison to invite the commander of another garrison to the meetings he holds to analyse the disciplinary situation in his garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The next document is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May that document be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D999, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D999 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exhibit 65 ter 1809, which is dated the 22nd of April, 1995, and it's a report, again, from Major Gojevic from the Knin garrison HQ, as its heading. His anticipated work plan for April. We've dealt with the types of issues here in previous questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn to page 2, in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The appointment of Major Marko Gojevic necessitates the employment of additional personnel at the garrison. And IN point 2, Knin garrison HQ sent archive material to the Military District, and they're organizing their document after they've sorted them. Again, this isn't covered in your report about the difficulties setting up these Knin garrisons, other garrisons, because of lack of personnel. Do you agree? You don't say, Look, the situation we have here is that garrisons started in 1993, they plainly face difficulties establishing themselves. When Knin was liberated on the 5th of August, the available evidence indicates that the previous acting commander of the Knin garrison had not been able to establish a garrison command as a functioning unit. You don't address the issue like that, do you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because as I have explained, the Knin garrison prior to Operation Storm cannot be defined as a functioning or regular garrison because it is not located in its normal zone of activity, and the municipalities that are to be covered by that garrison are still under control of the Serbs. So it wouldn't make, at least from a military point of view, make much sense to establish a Knin garrison command which has no zone of responsibility at that stage. The zone of responsibility only exists on paper, I mean, you have -- described in D33, Knin garrison covers the municipalities of Knin, Nadvode, Kistanje, Ervenik, Orlic, Kijevo, and Civljane. 24 Prior to Operation Storm, all these municipalities are under Serb control. There are no units of the HV present in these areas so the duties, for example, listed under paragraph 54 of the 1993 regulation do not apply, because they cannot be implemented. I'm just looking at the question if --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We've got the point on that --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And you have answered it for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D1000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1000 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a series of documents in exactly the same vein following this. There is no need to go through them, in my judgment. I think the Court is aware of the issue and has heard the witness's evidence on the matter, and it would be in the interests of justice to save time, but I would like the documents to be admitted because they go to my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, of course, they become bar table documents, I think the Chamber gave guidance as to how they should be introduced so that the chamber knows what is to specifically pay attention to and a brief description of -- and then a brief description of the content of the document or the -- what the document is about, then this to be shown to the other party to see whether there are any comments on that, so that if we receive the documents that we have guidance. And if, for example, a document is a ten-page document where you want us to focus especially on a subject dealt in the paragraph 6 and -- page 6 and 7, that we know where to primarily look at. So that guidance is still there. And with this proviso in view of the fact that Mr. Waespi has expressed no objections, they can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I was hoping to read out the 65 ter numbers, as they're all on the same issue and have them made exhibits straight away. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
