utterances.text: Well, reading out 65 ter numbers -- I think what the Chamber wants, is that if documents are introduced into evidence without by questioning a witness on a certain document, having drawn the attention of -- of what the purpose is of bringing this to the attention of the Chamber, that we have no objections as long as by other means, the same aim is achieved, so as to say if it's a one-page document, then of course just a description, Mr. X requesting support by military police for football match or for boxing match, or whatever, then it is clear. But if they are longer documents -- and just from the 65 ter numbers, we cannot see whether they're longer documents or not, whether we need specific guidance how to look at -- at this document for what purpose to look at that document, then we might easily miss the point you want to make with the documents. If they are in a series, I would not mind if I say six documents all the same, this is the purpose or this is the importance of the document, like garrison commanders, several garrison commanders reporting to headquarters or to whatever, so that we know what we are talking about and what to focus on, if we receive these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. What I propose to do is refer to the transcript where the evidence is taken place, and I think that would be of additional help. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There again I do not know whether these are one-page documents, whether they're all invitations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They're the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, looking at this document, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we get the point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say they're all -- and let me now just ... If you say these are all reports on the main, special, and regular tasks completed prior to Operation Storm from various garrison commanders or all of them by their Knin garrison headquarters, then we know what you want. Because that's the document which is in front of us at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. We've taken on board that guidance, and we will be dealing with it in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you get it in a short piece of paper then --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next matter I am going to ask you about concerns the passage in your report where you refer to the Split garrison commander, Colonel Zoricic, issuing disciplinary proceedings against military personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page would be, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, linking up footnotes with documents. 65 ter 5988, page 593, part 1. Footnote 593, part 1 of the report, page 175. And it's: Report on concluded disciplinary investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And as you have footnoted it, the sentence you are concerned with is: "Garrison commanders have the authority to order disciplinary investigations." And you produce this document as to that fact. Isn't that right, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you appreciate that the subject of the disciplinary investigation was, in fact, a subordinate within the Split garrison?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. And when I read again in my report, it could have assisted to include that reference. But I agree with you, that the subject is a member of the Split garrison command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And this is not the case of a wider use of disciplinary investigations, which your sentence in your report might have led people to believe. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm, I don't agree, because for -- I mean -- the system is that for every sentence, there is a footnote, and the references in the footnote show what the sentence is based on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It doesn't say that Petar Bilobrk, apologies to him for miss pronunciation of his name, was a lieutenant working at the Split garrison command, does it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I agree with you as I said earlier that the specific indication could have been included, but it doesn't change what is -- or it doesn't affect what I put in the report. Adding that he is a member of the Split garrison command would clarify or provide additional information, but doesn't change anything to the principle idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's have a look at that, shall we. A disciplinary investigation may be conducted by a commander in respect of his subordinates. Is that not right? Article 19 of the Code of Military Discipline, exhibit number -- I don't have the exhibit number, but it was 65 ter 1834, Article 19 of the Code of Military Discipline. Exhibit P1007 is the particular Article. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the Article in front of me, but, I mean, it's in line with the other contents of the -- of the Code of Discipline, P1007.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'll read it out, no need to put it on the screen as we will lose time: "Superior officers shall decide the disciplinary responsibility of their subordinates in accordance with prescribed procedure and shall hand down disciplinary measures as authorised by this Code." Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is no order, Article, saying that the garrison commanders order disciplinary investigations. That is a matter for the criminal section of the military police.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But when we look at the document on the screen, we can see by your decision, and "you" refers to the addressee, command of the Split garrison, I have been appointed to carry out an investigation in the violation of military discipline, and so on, and so on, and then the person who to conducted the investigation submits the report to the commander of the Split garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is it not a disciplinary investigation of someone who is not a subordinate of the garrison commander. That is the point, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then your previous question doesn't count. I think I have mentioned twice during the past over the previous questions that indeed, the entry in my report could have been clarified by adding disciplinary investigations of their subordinates. But of their, subordinates in my view, doesn't change anything to the principle that based on this document, the commander of a garrison can order a disciplinary investigation. And as I mentioned, I agree with you that I could have been more specific. I mean if I were to look at it again, I would probably add "against members of their units" just to clarify it because it appears that it has created some misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is limited to the garrison staff who were subordinated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, I think the matter is clear enough. If I read -- if I read 6 (A) and 6 (B) on page 175 which is apparently the issue we're talking about, and B starts with: "In March 1995 the Split garrison commander Zoricic, for example ... " I understood "for example" to be a reference to 6 (A), which I would say limits -- they have the duty to issue rules on order ... Let me just see. 6 (A) limits the behaviour of military personnel in the garrison. I understood this to be the garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It was pointed out me there may have been some ambiguities in this matter, in fact, from people watching, and I wanted to make sure that the point was clear. Thank you very much. I have other documents going further into Mr. Bilobrk at the garrison, but I have no need to produce those.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just like to clarify that 6(A) is a reference to, as the footnote states, Article 52 of D32, whereby the garrisons are defined as a geographic concept. The area covered by the garrison. Whereas this specific document is a disciplinary investigation of a member of the garrison command which is, of course, much more restricted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you would say 6(A) refers to issuing rules for the whole of the -- could I say the territory of the garrison; whereas, 6(B), I then -- be, for example, then comes as a surprise, because taking disciplinary action is, of course, something totally different from issuing rules on -- on military discipline. But the matter has been clarified. The example you give in (B) is the exercise of disciplinary power limited to those working in the garrison staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, the example refers to the -- the personal initiative by Colonel Zoricic to control the conduct of military personnel during the Ajax/Hajduk Split football game assisted by the military police, and then there's a full stop. So the next sentence is the sentence we're dealing with. And just to repeat, for example, is part of the first sentence under(B), and does not refer to the second sentence under --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So in (B) we find first an example of how the function to -- of being responsible, enforcing military discipline in the garrisons was exercised in the specific example.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then footnote 593 refers to a different matter which is where disciplinary action was taken not as a -- by way of a regulation or not by initiating supervision of certain conduct of larger groups, but one specific example. It's clear to me. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That finishes that particular matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May that document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1001, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1001 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to document 65 ter 2304.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document you're familiar with, Mr. Theunens. It's dated the 10th of August, 1995. It is P1134, Exhibit P1134. And we're now moving from pre-Oluja, Operation Storm, to documents post-Operation Storm. And this is a document from the security and information service to the central command, signed by the assistant commander Zeljko Pavic. You're familiar with this document, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it's included in my report, and it was also tendered during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You went through various aspects of it. Shall we go through to page 4. Just look at the information at this date. We see that there is an -- a paragraph -- ah, we've got different numbering.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May we go to the previous page, please. Previous one to that; I'm sorry. I'm looking at paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Relations and problems with UNCRO. And we need the next page. But we can just look at the last words there, with the arrival and appointment of General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Commander of the Knin garrison. "Direct contact was established with UN members stationed in Knin." In this document, there is an analysis by -- by SIS concerning those first days after Operation Storm. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But it also addresses the situation, for example, when elements of the Split Military District enter Knin. So during Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm actually interested in after, because General Cermak comes after, and some of those matters have been dealt with already. But that is in paragraph 5 where that is referred to.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, General Cermak is appointed on the -- on the 5th of August, and in my report I have included an order he issued already on the 5th, and formally Operation Storm finishes, I think, around the 9th or the 10th, just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're going to be looking at that order on the 5th of August as -- have you analysed the date on that order and how it could have been issued on the date it say it is? You're analyst. Have you analysed it, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The date?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We will look at it in due course. It's clear from this report, if we turn to paragraph 11, page 9 of my document. Yes. There we are. "According to our assessment, the establishment of civil authorities started in a disorganised and euphoric manner. There was no coordination with the current military authorities in the town following the arrival of civilian structures in Knin large groups of civilians roamed the town without control posing a security threat. The commander of the Knin ZM is overburdened with many problems and is not able to deal with them all successfully." Again this goes to the issue that I put to you several times concerning the ability of the Knin garrison to function properly as a unit after Operation Storm. Is there any reason why you didn't bring Their Honours's attention to this kind of information in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this paragraph can be found on -- in part 2 of the report, pages 262 and 263. In addition, I, of course, looked for documents showing General Cermak's views on his situation as the commander of the Knin garrison from the 5th of August till November 1995, and I have not come across a document in which General Cermak, for example, mentions that he has no ability to carry out his duties or that he lacks manpower, I mean, in significant numbers. There is a document where he orders the reassignment of one officer of the logistics base of the Split Military District to the Knin garrison command, but, again, I haven't seen any documents by General Cermak in which he expresses difficulties concerning the implementation of his duties, and I find that an important observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can go to 65 ter 2305. Exhibit D982. A document from the political activities department of Operation Group North. Problems and shortcomings perceived following the liberation of occupied areas. And we can see the various problems that are set out on this first page of the report, the various tasks that are being completed due to non-existence of the communication system in Knin, it became operational only today. Our communication was impeded. Instances of lack of maintaining contacts and coordination. Several individuals performing the same work at the same time. Problems with the civilian bodies looking at the issues there. If we go to paragraph 5, page 3 of 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And these are matters that you brought out in your report about the problems being faced at the time. "Activities of all civil structures are mainly reduced to making use of the right moment for individuals's appearance in the media ... unsatisfactory coordination of civil authorities has its roots in the incapacity of the government's commissioner for Knin whose organisational ability is not credible. He does not behave in accordance with the level of his responsibility, while, at the same time, he is involved in everything but his assignments." And we see down at the bottom who this document is to be delivered to. These issues, Mr. Theunens, in these documents, which are internal documents of the Croatian system, are very important in relation to identifying responsibility, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this specific document is discussed on page 263, part 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But from a military point of view, they're first and foremost important to inform the commander about the problems that exist and to encourage him to take action, if he is in a position to take action, or if is he not a position or has the authority to take action, to bring up these problems with those who are in a position to take action. So of course they also allow to determine responsibility, but in first instance such reports are intended to encourage the commander to take appropriate measures in order to sort -- solve these problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Isn't it important that in this report, the previous report that we've looked at, and another report to come, that there is no responsibility for problems laid at the door of Mr. Cermak? Not a single criticism that, within the scheme of things of what is happening, that he is failing to do his tasks?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned in my previous answer, this is not the first -- I mean, blaming people is not the first purpose of a military report, even though I agree with you, that is there is particular emphasis, for example, on Petar Pasic on members of the, call it, purely civilian authorities, whereas in relation to General Cermak it is stated in P1134 that the command of the Knin garrison is overburdened with many problems and is not able to deal with all of them successfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The previous document we looked at laid blame on the commanders who lost control of their men when they entered Knin, and we looked at that when you gave evidence a few days ago. I have pointed here to the civil aspect of it. You have made a statement in your expert report that Mr. Cermak is the most senior authority, civilian and military, in the area, and yet we are looking at internal reports that do not mention him as having failed in his responsibilities and duties on these matters that are being criticised by these organisations. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you have considered it to be fair in the production of your expert report to this Chamber to have pointed out that information to the Judges?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just reviewing page 262 to 264.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The internal documents do not hold Mr. Cermak responsible for the problems that are happening. Instead, they are sympathetic to him being overburdened.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And, of course, when we're talking about the aspect of responsibility, it is much easier to determine the responsibility of an operational commander if members of his units engage in the kind of activities that are described in paragraphs -- for example, 8 of this document, as -- I mean -- I'm talking now about P1134. I agree with you that there is no specific, call it blame or -- blame laid on General Cermak in -- in 1134, and also the document on the screen suggests the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at the next document, which is the third in this series, Exhibit D810, dated the 13th August, 1995. Again, from the department of political activity, the chief, Major-General Tolj who writes a report on that date. I believe this is a report you are familiar with. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, indeed. And I'm just looking where I mention it in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's in the same section that I have just been referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You're familiar with this. It's the passages concerning the churches.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And Mr. Misetic asked you questions. On page 3, we see that it is mentioned about fires being the largest a day or two following the entry of HV units into liberated villages. Killing of cattle. If we go to page 5, foreign and local journalists are mentioned. The paragraph after that: "The work that has been done most poorly and which is of vital significance of the return of displaced persons is the rounding up of cattle. At this juncture this should be one of the civilian organs of government's priority tasks. In Knin itself, civilian authorities have demonstrated weaknesses in organizing public utility services, et cetera." And we can see the text there. "Some of their work had to be completed by Croatian army services," which meant that they had to reduce some of their operation tasks in this report to Major-General Tolj by the coordinator Colonel Zelic. Again, same issue: The problems that being faced are frankly expressed in these reports concerning law and order as well as crimes that have been committed as well as problems, but none of them hold Mr. Cermak responsible. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But they do show a set of circumstances where it is understandable that a man of pragmatism would be needed in Knin to undertake tasks to get the city going. Don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, and in the document Zelic also states that "a number of incidents could have been reduced with better and more coordinated work between the civilian and military police and all structures of civilian and military government."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I believe that the word "government" should be authority, but I'm not going to pretend to be a linguist here. But military government, in my view, refers to military authority, and, yeah, that is in line with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Knin is entered on the 5th of August, and it had been a town within an area that had been very closed to the outside world since 1991. Don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And since the latter half of 1991, indeed, since the time it was under Serb control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It had been shut off from the outside world to a large extent. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But as I mentioned yesterday, that does not prevent those who are supposed to take over power in the area, be it civilian or military authority or the military commanders whose units are to operate in the area to do contingency planning prior to carrying out operations in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I quite agree. And as you know, General Cermak was appointed on the 5th of August and had not been responsible for any contingent planning. There's no evidence to that. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not -- I mean we have mentioned that he was appointed on the 5th. I have not seen any documents as to his activities immediately prior to the 5th of August or his involvement in any contingency planning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have got the documents as to what he was doing beforehand, and we will be looking at those, but you have given the answer on the other matter. Thank you. Would you accept that there was a realization on this matter after Operation Storm by the Chief of Staff, the Main Staff of the Croatian army, just on this matter that they needed to be better organised and have an aerial command imposed, or imposed isn't the right word to use, but better structures and organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at D559, Exhibit D559, which is the order from General Cervenko who was the Chief of Staff at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that what you were searching for?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. That is the order where General Cervenko mentions the establishment of area or garrison commands. It is mentioned on page 151 in part two of the report, and it's dated 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's have a look at this, because the point you raise about the lack of preparedness is something that I don't challenge. 14th of August, 1995, successful completion of Operation Storm. Conditions created for the establishment and functioning of all aspects of government of our state within its internationally recognised borders. We see the order there. The commands to the Military Districts being required to prepare and carry out the following main tasks in their areas of responsibility. Protection of the state border.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see the issues that are the concern of the Chief of Staff. If we go up from the bottom: "Urgent establishment of an aerial command. Structure that must be enabled to efficiently carry out tasks of a logistical nature. For this purpose, I particularly order: Immediately propose to the Chief of the Main Staff commanders and other personnel of the Military District commands in the liberated parts of the Republic of Croatia, who, by an order of the commander-in-chief, were assigned to the garrisons." And we see them named there and prescribed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if we turn to the next page, we see expedite the clearing up of the liberated areas [sic]. We see in according with the earlier order: Continue collecting and inspecting war booty ... warehousing ammunition ... assets, mines, explosives, logistics facilities. If we look through the rest of this document it is a reenforcement and preparation of combat units and Home Guard units with personnel, training of combat units. Page 7 has the Split Military District. And then if we get to page 8, we see that it is signed by General Cervenko and to whom it is sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And, of course, it is not sent to the Knin ZM? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Now if the Knin garrison was the superior military authority in the area, this document would have been sent to it, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. Only if the author of the order considered it important for the Split garrison command to receive the order. Excuse me, the Knin garrison command, I apologise. So if the author, i.e., the chief of the Main Staff, considered this particular order relevant for the Knin garrison command or had included instructions for the Knin garrison command --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let's look at it. In your report at paragraph 49, you say that General Cermak is the superior military and civil authority in the area. And we're now looking at a document, and there are many documents, aren't there, from the Chief of Staff issued before this period, none of which go to General Cermak. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may well be correct. But it also depends on the contents of documents. Orders are sent to those who are intended to implement the order. If the Knin garrison command is not among the organs or units or structures who are to implement the specific order, there is no need for them to receive the order. But again we would have to look at specific documents in order to be able to provide a more specific answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are many documents in this case, and the Judges will be able to look at them and take this point on board. I'm not going to go through every document now to make my point. But this document I selected because it refers to the garrisons and your barrister or counsel in presenting this matter referred to your Article 49 about Mr. Cermak being the superior authority, and all can you come up with is not necessarily it would -- that it would not be sent to the superior authority, General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the conclusion included in paragraph 49 of the executive summary is based on a review of the documents that address General Cermak's activities while he is the commander of the Knin garrison. As to why the order, D559, by General Cervenko, is not specifically sent to the commander of the Knin garrison, I have answered that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, I'm a bit puzzled by your language where you said your barrister or counsel, was that in relation to this expert, because I'm not aware of this expert being anything else than appearing as an expert before this court called by the Prosecution. The Prosecution is represented by counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, Your Honour. It's just that Mr. Theunens works for the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that should not be confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There we are. That's that document that deals with that. And let's go to the document that follows on, 65 ter 2093. So the document D559, Exhibit D559 we've been looking at which you are familiar with, has a follow-up document, 65 ter 2093. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. It is the order by General Gotovina, which follows from the order of General Cervenko, and it is discussed on pages 157 and 158 of part 2, and I'm referring to English pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. This is dated the 20th of August, 1995. It's from General Gotovina. Order on the operative deployment of HV units and commands. And we can see on page 1, it actually sets out, if we can scroll down the page, the same matters that General Cervenko did: Protection of the state border.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Routing of lagging enemy groups and mopping up. Guarding of roads and communications. Urgent establishment of a territorially based command, which shall be enabled to efficiently execute the logistics tasks. For that purpose, I hereby command. The Home Guard, in cooperation with the personnel affairs to submit proposals to him for commanders and other officers for the garrison commands, which, in the liberated areas, which have been defined as garrisons, Benkovac, Knin, mentioned. Next page: "To speed clearing up the terrain." Dealing with the logistics. And just stopping there, that is because the garrison is primarily a logistics base, as a concept in the military. Isn't it, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not correct. The Split Military District has a -- has its logistics base. It's 306th Logistics Base, and even though the garrison can assist in logistical issues or matters, logistics is according to the doctrine, both in Croatian armed forces as well as in other armies, not -- predominantly an organisation that is preoccupied with logistics. And if you want, I can explain why I draw that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. You have given your answer. And the next page, page 4. We're dealing here of -- to establishing an efficient defence of the state border, area of responsibility. We can see on page 4 orders for the protection of facilities of interest to the state, military and economy. Operative reserve being deployed in barracks, and it's to be delivered to -- and if we look on the next page, we can see the recipients of this which do not include the Benkovac and Knin ZM garrisons. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is -- I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if, as you describe, Mr. Cermak was the superior commander in Knin, he would have received a document like this, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I used the wording the highest military/civilian authority, which is not necessarily the same as the superior commander. And I think the point you raise illustrates what I called that the -- the lack of clarity in the relation between Generals Gotovina and General Cermak, i.e., that the relation between the two of them, professional relation, is not as clear-cut as is established in the doctrine, whereby, according to doctrine, garrison commanders are subordinate to Military District Commanders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please point at where you use that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In paragraph 49.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 49, I see that. When you are describing the areas covered whether it is civilian, military authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And then it goes Cermak is the most senior authority in Knin, superior to the military police --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And civilian police in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you want to change that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because, as I mentioned earlier, I draw that conclusions on orders issued by General Cermak as well as subsequent orders by, for example, the civilian police following an order by General Cermak. I just drew your attention to the fact that I didn't use the expression "commander," I used the term "authority."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is probably a convenient moment for the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is, Mr. Kay. We will resume at five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, just taking up on the last matter that we were discussing, page 241 of your report -- sorry, I've forgotten the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've forgotten to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I've forgotten the exhibit number of the report, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, have I the report constantly on my screen, so the page -- the expert report of Mr. Theunens. Oh, for the registrar, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Page 241. And in this section of the report, we can see (A), you're focussing on the role as the civilian and military role in Knin. And in (C), you indicate within this Exhibit P1113, a review of military documentation between the 6th of August and 15th of November, indicates Cermak's duties covers two areas, civilian/military authority, and then you refer to a number of matters, including law and order. We've considered your earlier three drafts to that final report, and in each one of those earlier three drafts, you describe General Cermak as being the civilian authority in Knin. Your third draft taking it as the last one, at page 257, heads the section as this: "This section describes the duties of Colonel General Cermak during the time-period is he commander of the Knin garrison, focussing on his role as civilian authority in Knin." "A review of military documentation" - this at paragraph (C) - "between 6th August and 5th November 1995 indicates that Cermak's duties cover two areas: Civilian authority and point of contact for the international community." We will go before I ask you specifically about it. Final report, page 245. So Exhibit P1113, page 245, paragraph 2, a review of military documentation covering Cermak's role as commander of Knin garrison. Same period we have looked at. First bullet point: "Civilian/military authority, including all aspects of the normalisation of the conditions of life in the area, return of displaced persons and refugees. Law and order situation of Serbs in UNCRO barracks." Bullet point: "Point of contact for international community. (B), civilian/military authority from the date he is appointed to the position of the commander of the Knin garrison." In each of the previous three drafts of your report, first draft, page 117; second draft, page 117; third draft, page 261; Mr. Cermak is described as the civilian authority. What I want to ask you, Mr. Theunens, is this: What happened for your final report that changed your previous opinion in the drafts, from civilian authority to civilian/military authority? Why did your position change, for your final draft for these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it so much as a change in position. I think the fact that you have read out different page numbers, 117, 261 and now actually we're looking at page 245 in the version of the report, the final version that has been filed. It has to do with reviewing the material. There may have been additional material that became available. I have also reviewed the report obviously in order to try to clarify certain issues which may not have been entirely clear. That was especially the case when I drafted the summaries for each and every section, which I did at the very end for logical reasons and then use these summaries to compile the executive summary. So it may -- or it probably was the case that the qualifications civilian authority, looking at all the material I considered for the report, is, in my view, not entirely correct, and that's why I included also the military aspect, i.e. -- I put civilian/military authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I tell you that in this section of the final report that you did not use any further documents from the documents that you had used previously in draft number three?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is -- that is possible. And then we refer to the second part of my answer to the previous question, that is, that when I reviewed the report, you will probably have noticed that the structure sometimes changed. Some headings changed. And I see the inclusion of the "/military" as one of the changes I made during that process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have discussions with any other members of the OTP about these conclusions in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no discussion about the conclusions. The -- when I sent the final draft to Mr. Tieger, and I'm not sure anymore, I think it was in November. I mean, I don't recall the exact date. He asked me a number of questions about certain aspects whether they could be clarified or what they really meant or not, but there was no change or there was no request by Mr. Tieger to change any conclusions or to change the contents of the report. The only questions or -- or -- or requests I remember was about, for example, location of certain parts of the report in order to streamline the -- the layout.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If not discussions, was there any other influence upon you to change your drafts so that your final report included the military dimension to Mr. Cermak's responsibility?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And, again, I'm not sure whether I understand the question, but there was no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any doubt about the question, simply this: Was any line on which the words "civilian authority" appear in drafts, which was subsequently changed in "civilian/military authority" whether it would be in the executive summary, whether it would be on whatever page, was that ever referred to or mentioned or quoted, or was that ever part of any conversation you had with any member of the Office of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not to my recollection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In that section I put to concerning page 245, also inserted in the final report which is not in the drafts is the phrase "law and order." How did it come about that you changed your position to insert that concept of "law and order" into your final report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned, I see these changes not as fundamental changes or changes in conclusions or changes in positions. I see these changes as a, call it, a streamlining of the contents of the report. It is correct that the discussion I referred to -- I mean, the discussions with Mr. Tieger, addressed several parts of the report. This part of the report, I think, if I remember well, was also part of it. But it's not that I suddenly invented a title: Law and order, where as I had no material to support that conclusion or that comment. As you see from the structure and mainly the contents of the report, the titles or the headings reflect what follows afterwards, and the material that is included in the body of the report has indeed changed over time because I had access or I had the opportunity to review more documents. And obviously while reviewing more documents, it could be that in some situations a conclusion changed, but I have no specific recollection of that. It could also that be a heading changed just for the -- for the sake of clarifying or streamlining the report or coming back to the discussions or the meetings with Mr. Tieger after the submission to him of the final draft, that he asked me to clarify what I meant because, as have you noticed, I'm not a native speaker, so some things may have lacked clarity to native speakers. So, therefore, there was a discussion about what do you mean by that, what do you want to say, without any suggestion to me about what I should put in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, in this section of the final report, which is the garrison section, the documents that you used in your final draft were the same ones that you'd used in your final report, so there'd been no change in the materials that you used.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the second time you asked that question, and I have already provided an answer to the question. If you want me to elaborate further, I noticed that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, I said it, because you said you had the opportunity to review more documents. And obviously while reviewing more documents, so I was actually dealing with something that you had said, Mr. Theunens, and I'm not repeating a question, I'm actually saying, Well, hang on, you have said this, but actually the documents remain the same.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- as I mentioned in my previous answer to the same question, I made that -- I said that in the general context of the report. You mentioned yourself page numbers. You noticed that these page numbers changed. One of the reasons for the change in page numbers is that additional material was included structure was changed, and so on, and on so on. I was giving a general answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm concerned about this section --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To provide clarification to my attempt to answer the previous question, when I reviewed the documents that are relevant in the context of -- of General Cermak's role as the commander of the Knin garrison, and I specify here, in particular, his orders, one of my immediate conclusions was that his role was much wider than what was established in the doctrine of the Croatian armed forces in relation to the duties of garrison commanders. I must say that I was also -- it was unclear to me at that stage in the beginning when I was reviewing the material whether General Cermak was a military authority a civilian authority. It was clear that he was doing more than a garrison commander. I saw, for example, and he mentions that in the press interview he gave, D38, that he talks about a Petar Pasic, who, according to General Cermak, was to begin with the establishment of the civilian organisation of government on 16th of August. Well, I did searches on Petar Pasic, and I found very little documents on him except for a number of ECMM reports which were from much later than the time-period relevant in the context of the report. So I had this material on General Cermak, and then I tried to structure it and to find -- to identify headings as to how I should describe his role, and it may well be that in the earlier drafts, I put civilian authority. But it is obvious from when you review, when you look at the material included in this section of the report that General Cermak also carries out duties that fall under somebody who has military authority, and that explains, in my view, why the heading changed from "civilian authority" to "civilian/military authority."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it seems it wasn't obvious to you in your first three drafts. Don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again they are drafts. Whether I had changed the headings already at that stage -- as I mentioned at the very beginning of my testimony, conclusions or the main conclusions were drawn by me at the end. Why? Because only at the end I was in a position to -- yeah, to draw conclusions because then -- I had been able to review all the material I wanted to review. Not in the beginning, because then I was starting with the review. It may be purely for logistics that headings of documents -- sorry, headings of sections of the report were only systematically reviewed by me at a later stage, and even I may have changed headings, some headings earlier and others later. I have no specific recollection of which heading I changed at which time and even whether there was -- what the specific reason for that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The questions that Mr. Tieger gave you, did they include questions that referred to Mr. Cermak being a military authority?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say the questions that Mr. Tieger gave you, do you refer to the 10- and then the 17-point lists?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, no. No. What Mr. Tieger communicated to you that you told us about.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After your third draft, did that concern questions relating to Mr. Cermak having military authority?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger didn't specifically give me questions. I remember that there was at least one meeting between him and myself in his office where we went through certain aspects, parts of the report. He also pointed out certain typos, and he may -- he asked me to clarify certain aspects of the report including also probably certain headings, or asked me, Well, what do you mean by that? As I mentioned, Mr. Tieger never suggested to me which heading or which conclusion I was to draw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But did that include the discussion with you that Mr. Cermak had the military authority as well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, you haven't. No, you haven't. You have answered other questions, and you have raised other matters, and you've got more focussed in relation to these matters, and you've said that he raised matters concerning the report. Did that include Cermak, in relation to military authority?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- it did not include Cermak in relation to military authority specifically. We did indeed discuss the -- the general layout or structure of this section. I mean, the section number 3. But as I mentioned, Mr. Tieger did not suggest or -- or propose or influence me otherwise in relation to the choice of headings or the -- the drawing of conclusions. He may have asked me or he probably asked me, What do you mean by this? What are you trying to say? Maybe this word is better, but -- I mean, when I say this word is better, it is a linguistical issue. I'm not a native speaker. That is it. I think I have reiterated it three or four times during the past minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, if you would allow me. Would this be the versions that we're talking about? That is, you had a discussion with Mr. Tieger not after having sent the first draft which was within the deadline, but at a later stage, and then you had a communication with Mr. Tieger about that. Could I take you back to one of the answers, and I will read it slowly and carefully to you, and I'm quoting page 12159. You said that: "I knew that March 2007 was withdrawn, but I had not received information for the new deadline which I find a bit difficult in a sense, as I was working on several cases. I tried to organise my work and, of course, what is more urgent, you try to do first. What is less urgent, you do later. So that is why I'm sent him - apparently you're talking about Mr. Tieger - more drafts in order to keep him updated of the progress I made, and I don't remember receiving any feedback on these other drafts I sent." Then you were asked: "Well, Mr. Tieger and Mr. Moore did, in fact, give you feedback on your table of contents and approved that table of contents; didn't they?" And then you explained that that was -- the table of contents was in January. Then you explain about -- I'm just trying to find where you said, in -- only feedback was the deadline does not apply. Please continue. I'm just trying to remember where you, at that stage, told us that you had discussions with Mr. Tieger, as you described them now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I received feedback for the last draft, which I think was sent in November or early December --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you to assist me in where you said this when you were questioned about this on -- on 19th November. I may have missed it, but then please assist me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know exactly when on the 19th I said it. There were many questions in relation to similar issues. But I have a recollection that I said that I received feedback only for the last draft.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the case, I might have missed. If the parties could assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, our position is that I don't think that was disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I had no contact with the team. I also want to emphasise that except for the initial tasking I received from Mr. Tieger and the sending of the draft, I had no contact with the team. I didn't receive any phone calls. I didn't receive any -- or e-mails. I heard when I insisted when I sent the draft in, March 2007, I'm not sure anymore how I was informed that, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll carefully check this, Mr. Theunens, and I'm cautious now in my wording. But if it would turn out that you were questioned quite in detail as to feedback and where you clearly testified that the only reason why you sent them is to keep them updated on what progress you made, rather than to receive any feedback. And where specific questions were put to you, I just read a portion of it where you said, No, that was all in that January. Clearly questions focussing on feedback that you may have received or further conversations you may have had, if that would turn out the situation, then I would like to remind you that you gave a solemn declaration, not only that would you speak the truth, nothing but the truth, but also the whole truth. Please proceed, Mr. Kay. If I'm mistaken, and, of course, we will check that carefully, but unfortunately we're not in a position to analyse it. I did quite a few searches, and it is your experience that now and then if you do a search that you miss something. If I missed something, then, of course, I'll -- I'll -- we'll clearly express my regret if I did that. The parties are invited to join me in the exercise I tried to undertake. Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For the record the passage I read from was 12158.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, may I have the last order that we produced before the break, 65 ter 2093, be admitted please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit D1002, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1002 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter 755. It's a document dated the 25th of August. It's from the 4th Guards Brigade commander, Brigadier Krsticevic - apologies again - and this document concerns an order issued on the 20th of August, 1995, concerning the units at the state border with Bosnia and is in order to ensure an effective operational deployment of units and commands of the 4th Guards Brigade. And it's an order that we see on page 1, refers to operational reserve of the 4th Guards Brigade, under the Military District Commander. If we go to page 2, we see the operational area of responsibility. In point 2, further down the page, we see that the units of the 4th Guards Brigade operationally deployed various sections in Knin. If we go to page 3, the signals are in barracks in Knin, logistics in barracks in Knin. Page 4 gives details concerning the taking over of buildings, warehouses, et cetera. Page 5 at .34, commander of the Knin barracks, Major Turic, preparing a plan for the deployment of units in the Sjeverni Logor barracks, which we know are in the Knin, making commanders responsible for the premises. Prohibited, at the bottom of the page, to store weapons, ammunition, explosives. And the last page, we see it's from the Brigadier, as I said, to whom it's sent, and not including the Knin garrison. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if Mr. Cermak was the superior military authority in the area, this is the sort of detail that he would have to know, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, General Cermak should, as the garrison commander, should have been informed of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And, again, all these orders from the Split Military District of which there are many, aren't there, Mr. Theunens, of a similar nature, do not copy in Mr. Cermak as the garrison commander of Knin.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have included 65 ter 2315 on -- in part 2, English page 260, which is an order by General Gotovina, on the 10th of August, for part of the 7th Guards Brigade to be accommodated in the barracks in Knin, and I mention in my report no mention is made of General Cermak in General Gotovina's order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Again, this -- this rather defies that proposition, doesn't it, Mr. Theunens, concerning Mr. Cermak's authority and position, because he would be copied in on all these documents, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He should have been copied in, but the fact that General Gotovina does not -- or -- I apologise, subordinate commanders of General Gotovina do not include General Cermak in these orders was, for me, an indication that the professional relationship between General Cermak as the garrison commander and General Gotovina as the Split Military District commander, is not as I use the expression "clear-cut" as is established in the doctrine. My conclusion in relation to the position of General Cermak as the most senior civilian/military authority in Knin is based on a review of the orders issued by General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will be looking at those, and the Judges have seen all those orders already and know what you refer you. But you told us you're an expert on command and control, and the question I have is this: If all this is happening and all these orders are being issued, it doesn't seem that the man you described as being the superior military authority is within the command and control system. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that is why I have included this section on the nature of the professional relations between the commander of the Split Military District and the commander of the Knin garrison, starting on page 258 of the second part of the report. Even independently of the position of General Cermak as -- what I described as the most senior military authority in Knin, even as a garrison commander, with a -- at a much lower military rank than the rank of Colonel General, one would expect that, at least in according with the doctrine, he, as the garrison commander, would have been included in orders that deal with the relocation of units to barracks in the zone of the Knin garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, in relation to all these units, you couldn't have effective command if you're outside the system, if the system is not working with you in it as a component commander, could you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But I have not put in my report that General Cermak has command over these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. That's right. But you have read the indictment, and you may have forgotten the indictment, and the indictment at paragraph 7 describes Ivan Cermak as possessing effective control over members of the HV units or elements who comprised or were attached to or operated in the Knin garrison and also over the civilian police who operated in the garrison area. And then it describes the HV units without limitation. The 4th, 7th Brigades, 1st Croatian Guards Brigade, 113th, 142nd, 144th, 126th Home Guard. The 6th, and 7th, 134th, a combined military police company, members of the Zadar-Knin-Kotar police administrations. I appreciate the civilian area is outside in a way that you are positioned. But looking at all these Military District documents, we've looked at a few here which go to a particular issue, but there are, as you know, thousands in relation to all those units, General Cermak is -- is copied in on a handful of matters; isn't he?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, and I think it is visible through my report that there are very few orders by General Gotovina to the Knin garrison command or the Knin garrison commander during the time-period General Cermak is the commander of the Knin garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: My question is about General Cermak having effective control over all those units. They're all operating every day, in relation to their activities, where they go, what they do, completely independently and without General Cermak. That's right, isn't it? What I'm putting to you is that paragraph 7 on this indictment doesn't fit with your expert's report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may well be possible. I mean, I haven't -- I read the indictment once, as I mentioned, at the very start of the -- the report project, in order to determine time-frame, locations, and other relevant aspects. Otherwise, I have not been influenced or was bound any way by what is in the indictment. My findings or my conclusions in relation to the role of General Gotovina as the Knin garrison commander are included in my report and more specifically in paragraphs 49 to, I believe, 51 of the executive summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I hesitate to say you demoted General Gotovina to the garrison commander.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That would be controversial.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should read Cermak. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. But what I'm putting to you is right. On that passage of the indictment that I read out in relation to paragraph 7 which asserts that Ivan Cermak possessed in various structures of power and responsibility and possessed effective control over all those units - they're all the Split Military District units that we are familiar with - is, in fact, not borne out by your expert's report, and, indeed, all the documents that you have seen. It's right, isn't it? I'm right.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, I haven't addressed effective control, and I haven't seen any material or, I mean, documents on that aspect concerning the role of General Cermak as the commander of the Knin garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have had a note that Mr. Misetic needs to address you urgently, and if I just ask that document 65 ter 755 be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit D1003, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1003 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Misetic, you want to address us in the presence of the witness or in the absence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, the presence is fine. It wasn't urgent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it fine, or do we need him? [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... it's a document that he prepared, so I don't have a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it directly relates to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It wasn't urgent. I was just -- it follows on the discussion we had before this line of questioning. I did not wish to interrupt Mr. Kay while he was cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Another matter. How much time would it take?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Less than three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Less than three minutes, and it cannot wait until the last three minutes of today's session? If you think it is better positioned here, then I'll let you go, I will trust that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yeah. I was waiting for Mr. Kay to change -- to be ready to change topics before I raised this. It relates to the issue before that you had raised about Mr. Theunens prior testimony on communications with the Office of the Prosecutor. And if Mr. Randunic would be so kind, I would like to show something via sanction which is -- the Gotovina Defence asked for -- asked the OTP to disclose communications that had been had between members of the trial team and Mr. Theunens. We were given a report on the 12th of November, and if we could show that via sanction. This is it the disclosure. It is a 24-page document. It says that -- it's pursuant to our request. If we then turn to the next page, this is an apparently --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I first read the first page so that I know what is offered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, please. This appears to have been prepared by Mr. Theunens himself and signed on 11th November of this year, and it discloses certain communications. It talks again about January of 2007, and then it refers to the next communication identified as in paragraph 5 which is a communication from Mr. Tieger about new documents, and that memo is disclosed further on in this disclosure. And there are no other references or disclosures to -- in response to our inquiry about any communications that were had about changing, clarifying matters in the report, et cetera, and that this occurred after the third -- submission of the third draft. So I would request, Mr. President, that in addition to us reviewing the transcript from last week if -- if the Office of the Prosecutor would, in fact, go back and tell us exactly what transpired and what communications, in fact, were had because we thought we had resolved this matter pursuant to this communication from the Office of the Prosecutor and based on what Mr. Theunens has said today in Court, I think that this disclosure is incomplete. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, I think the question is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure this disclosure here addresses oral communications between Mr. Tieger and -- and the expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... could we go back to the first page to see how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will just point out paragraph 1 on page 2, Mr. Theunens discloses what appears to be a meeting that took place which would not be a written, as I understand it, a written communication. It was a meeting between the two STAs. So I, when I got this, assumed that Mr. Theunens was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... a discussion is described. This was followed by a discussion, so therefore apparently this -- this document does not limit itself to -- and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Our understanding, my understanding was that what the issue was, was the tasking. Original tasking of the expert. That's what the Defence was interested in, and we asked Mr. Theunens to address that. We looked at the e-mail communications that appeared to be relevant under this heading and the other issues about communications, oral communications, whether phone meetings, that is something that the expert can be cross-examined about, and that's exactly what happened. We were never hiding any piece of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cross-examination has taken place on this issue already, as you may be aware of. Could I have again the first page in which ... Of course the Chamber has not seen the e-mail of the 4th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can display that. I believe it would just take a minute but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But there's another question, of course. Mr. Waespi. You were present when quite a lot of questions were put to the witness which certainly were not limited to written communications but were about feedback and not limited in any way or form. I had on my mind to address you in the absence of the witness at the very end of this -- of this session, but since the issue more or less has been raised and in view of what we find here, I would ask you to carefully review the transcript, all the questions and all the answers that we find in the transcript, and then to also ask you to consider whether it would have been within your duties to specifically ask the witness on conversations at a rather late stage, where, if that's the case, if such a conversation has taken place, no one could know about it, perhaps certainly not on the basis of this document, whereas the Office of the Prosecution, the team, could have known about it, and should consider whether it would have left the Chamber without relevant information, where questions were specifically asked to Mr. Theunens in this respect. Well, that request, now that invitation is now with you anyhow. The e-mail, you said perhaps we can do it within a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I can read it to you briefly, Your Honour. It is correct that because our request had to be pursuant to Rule 66(B), which by definition, seeks documentation, it says, we hereby request a copy of all communications between OTP and Mr. Konings and Theunens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Yes, and you say the conversation cannot be copied.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right. So nevertheless, when we got the -- one of the -- I will tell you this by way of background. I had a conversation with Mr. Russo recently because they did produce e-mail communications between Mr. Konings, who will testify next week, and the OTP, but did not wish do disclose the e-mail communications between Mr. Theunens and members of the trial team. And in my conversations which would have then perhaps enabled us to cross-examine Mr. Theunens about meetings and stuff like that that would have been evident from e-mail communication. Mr. Russo represented to me that the problem that OTP was having was the fact that the volume and the having to search various individuals e-mails was unduly burdensome on them and that there was nothing of any substance in the e-mails, and that was a representation that he made, and I relied on that, as well as disclosure on the 12th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you have addressed us. That's what you wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do the other parties want to add anything to that before we continue? Then, Mr. Kay, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we go do 65 ter 370, and this was a document you referred to, Mr. Theunens, about the appointment of a garrison commander at Benkovac. And I promised you we'd get there. 4th of August, 1995, the appointment is made by the commander, Colonel Fuzul. And the heading is: On the basis of a need for best quality organisation and a coordinated establishment of civilian authority, I hereby make a proposal ... appointment of commander of Benkovac garrison HQ, Captain Ashley Minak." You were going to draw our attention to something in relation to this appointments, and I said to that you we would be looking at the document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, this is a proposal, and there is also a -- an order by General Gotovina --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We'll be looking at that next.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall we pull that up next. But what I'd like to look at here actually is best quality organisation, coordinated establishment of civilian authority, which are obviously important concepts; don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. 65 ter 4621 is the next document. It's an order dated the 6th of September, 1995 by General Gotovina. And it's due to frequent needs and for the purpose of ensuring continuity in operations and command of Split Military District units. And we see that Ashley Minak, a captain, is appointed Benkovac garrison commander. And he is to take over from Ante Maksan, who is the present garrison commander, immediately to be completed on the 9th of September. And Colonel Fuzul was responsible for the implementation of the order. On page 2 of the English we see who is copied into it. Again, no Knin ZM is the point that I would point out. What did you wish to draw your attention to with this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that General Gotovina appoints a replacement for an existing garrison commander. The fact that it's not sent to the Knin garrison command is not unusual because, as I pointed out earlier, the Benkovac garrison is a separate unit from the Knin garrison as are the other garrisons that are located in the zone of responsibility of the Split Military District, so there is no requirement to send an order for actually a transfer of authority for one particular garrison to the commanders of other garrisons of that Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I don't disagree with you on that. The reason why I pointed out is because of that paragraph 7 you and I have just looked at from the indictment. But I don't disagree with what you have told us about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May 65 ter 370 and 65 ter 4621 be admitted into evidence, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 370 becomes Exhibit D1004. 65 ter 4621 becomes Exhibit number D1005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1004 and D1005 are admitted into evidence. Before we move into our next subject, Mr. Kay, I wonder whether we should not adjourn for the day, but if you would give me one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we have a procedural matter to very briefly discuss but not necessarily in your presence. We'd like to see you back tomorrow afternoon, and I give you the same instructions as I gave you all the other days; that is, that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether given already or still to be given.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, I didn't want to further discuss the matter in the presence of the witness, but I looked at some of your statements in this courtroom, and I'm taking you back to page 12125, last line, you said: "Second, this was, as we explained, a work in progress. Yes, a draft was submitted to the Prosecution team at one time. There was no, absolutely no inference from the Prosecution team to the expert about changing anything. I'm not aware of any substantive changes. If there was inference from the Prosecution into the way that the expert drafted his report, advanced it after the draft, we would have disclosed it under Rule 68, that's for sure. That's our obligation." Now I leave totally apart whether the report ever changed in a way where the earlier draft would have been exculpatory. I refrain from any assessment at this moment about that. However, if I look at your statement, and if I read again the answers of the witness, and I sincerely hope I that have overlooked something. If not, then it's at least worrying the Chamber. The transparency which we would expect might not be given. Therefore, you are really invited to report tomorrow on the matter, on any follow-up discussions with -- between Mr. Theunens and Mr. Tieger. And also perhaps an explanation why you have not raised that issue once you had heard the answers the witness gave, which was an answer, and now I'm summarizing, that there was a discussion after the 10-point tasking, after there had been discussions before, that this resulted in the 17-points tasking, and that, later on, sending drafts was merely an administrative matter to keep you updated that there was no risk that finally the report would not be received but feedback, interfering with and -- nothing of this kind we should even think about. Now on the basis of the answers the witness gave today, it looks as if we do have to think about these matters. I am not saying what it resulted in, what the impact was, but the Chamber would like to receive in the absence of the witness tomorrow a short report on behalf of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, what I can only say at this time is I believe that there is a certain misunderstanding. I think what the issue was at that time, I think on the 19th of November, was the submission of the draft in March 2007, and that's what I led in evidence what kind of communication there was between Mr. Theunens and the trial team, and you quoted correctly what happened there. What Mr. Theunens now talked about today, and I'll address that as well, is after the final report his final product was submitted to the trial team, and then apparently there were discussions as pointed out by Mr. Theunens about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
