utterances.text: Was that after the final report had been --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the understanding, or was it just before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just before. After Mr. Theunens submitted his final report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Draft.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Final. Except for typos, it was finished, and then the trial team looked over it, and as Mr. Theunens testified, Mr. Tieger apparently asked him to clarify a couple of headings. There were typos. That is what I understand happened in, I think, November and December 2007. But expect, Mr. President, that perhaps even that part, I should have, could have led life, and I will look into that issue. But I think there are two very distinct issues: The conversation between expert and trial team in March 2007 when certainly the last -- the fifth draft was produced, and what happened after the final final product was delivered from Mr. Theunens to the trial team. That is the understand I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, my understanding is that he talking about November 2007, which is one month before the final final was filed. So the final brief was filed I believe the 17th or 18th of December of 2007, which means any conversations he had with Mr. Tieger would have been before the submission of the final final report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Theunens was so kind to provide you with you the draft. The chamber has not seen them. The Chamber doesn't know about dates of these drafts. So, therefore, whether there was a final version that was finally filed, unchanged, or whether there was a version which was discussed and then resulted in another final version, that's for the Chamber a bit difficult at this moment to assess on the basis of the information we have. But, at least the witness testified that he wanted to emphasise that except for the initial tasking he received from Mr. Tieger, and the sending of the draft, I had no contact with the team, which of course perhaps we should ask him more details about -- about this. But you will understand, Mr. Waespi, that it worries the Chamber and, of course, without having any contact with the witness, the Chamber would like to receive all information the OTP has on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. And in relation to that draft which was produced to the trial team a month prior to the official filing, I'm sure that this draft will be available to see any changes that were made pursuant to -- to talks between Mr. Tieger and the expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that the important issue is whether at a stage where, still, the final draft -- I do understand that once it's there when it has been presented that it is not filed within five minutes. Of course, that's -- of course, the Prosecution introduces it, and that may take some time. But what we, of course, want to know is that at any stage where changes like civilian, military, were still being made and Mr. Kay has, of course -- we have not received the earlier drafts, but at least it is not contradicted. It is it even confirmed by the witness that he said, well, in the earlier versions, we find civilian. I want to know whether there has been any contact, conversation, e-mail, I would exclude telepathic, but any other communication between the team, members of the team, assistants to the team, and this witness on the content, whether it is titles, whether it's structure, whether it's footnotes, whether it's numbering, whether such communication has taken place at all. That's what we'd like to receive, your report on tomorrow, at the beginning of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And that relates to the final product filed the last months between the submission of Mr. Theunens's report about end of October/November and December, that period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about a period. Let me just check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, our position would be that there really is no need to put a date on it. Whatever conversations were had about substance of the report, they should be disclosed to us. Or any communications about any substantive in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn for the day with our apologies for interpreters. Let me also include security. Always forget them. Interpreters, transcribers. We adjourn, and we'll resume tomorrow, the 3rd of December, quarter past two, in this same courtroom, I.
